primitives.name: Sensory Nudity
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is reduced, by this new way of attending to it, to its sensational nudity.
primitives.assumptions: Perception is decomposable into sensory and semantic components; sensory component is invariant under semantic overlay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When semantic associations are stripped, S becomes isolated from N.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Sensory data kernel extracted via semantic deconstruction. GSE: State transition triggered by sensory nudity.

primitives.name: Semantic Cloud
primitives.verbatim_quote: We apprehended it, in short, with a cloud of associates, and thus perceiving it, we felt it quite otherwise than as we feel it now divested and alone.
primitives.assumptions: Perception is influenced by associative memory networks; P varies inversely with C.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C is removed, P reduces to baseline sensory input.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Semantic cloud maps to contextual uncertainty in Bayesian inference. GSE: Cloud acts as cognitive load affecting decision states.
layer2.telemetry: Variation in perceptual consistency across contexts.

primitives.name: Inverted Perception
primitives.verbatim_quote: Another well-known change is when we look at a landscape with our head upside down.
primitives.assumptions: Visual perception is sensitive to orientation; I introduces D through neural reprocessing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At I=1, normal perception; at I=-1, inversion-induced distortion.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Inversion induces a transformation matrix in sensory space. GSE: Distortion triggers adaptive behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation in spatial judgment under inverted viewing.

The core insight is that perception operates in two regimes: one where sensory data is embedded within semantic clouds, and another where it is stripped bare. The sensory nudity primitive formalizes this stripping process, allowing for a clean separation of raw stimulus from interpretation. The semantic cloud primitive models how prior knowledge distorts perception, creating a non-linear relationship between stimulus and experience. Inverted perception shows that even simple geometric transformations can induce qualitative shifts in cognition, suggesting that perception is not merely passive but actively restructured by physical orientation. These primitives form a triadic structure: sensory input → semantic overlay → perceptual distortion. Their interplay defines the epistemic boundaries of perception, where failure modes arise from misalignment between sensory fidelity and interpretive frameworks.
